children: Wall Street sold off Wednesday after the Federal Open Market Committee delivered a 25-basis-point interest-rate hike, while policymakers signaled that another increase could come before year-end.

Jones noted that the rate increase marked the first hike in three years and said the unanimous vote suggested the threshold for another increase may not be particularly high.

He pointed to continued inflationary pressures, including diesel prices reaching an all-time high, which he attributed largely to the war against Iran. Jones also cited broader inflation trends that have remained elevated. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said, “The plain fact is that inflation is too high, and has been for too long,” according to Jones.
With inflation still above the Fed’s longer-term target and economic conditions showing weakness, Jones argued that the combination increasingly resembles stagflation.
“I have been arguing since August of last year that we are heading toward a stagflationary recession,” he said, adding that the case becomes “more compelling” each day.
